ELEC5360.d: The aim of this course is to provide an in-depth treatment of the theoretical basis, analysis, and design of digital communication systems. The first half of the course will focus on the theoretical foundations of a basic digital communication system, including source coding, modulating and channel coding, and introductory information theory. The second half will deal with advanced techniques including orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), multi-antenna communications, spread-spectrum communications, and cooperative communications.
cl: Comprehend M-ary digital modulation schemes.
Identify the fundamental principles related to digital communication technology.
Comprehend digital communications transmission over fading channels.
Comprehend technical specifications and understand how and why practical digital communications systems are designed.

ELEC5380.d: This course introduces state-of-the-art development in the interplay between information theory, data compression, and machine learning, including source coding theory, deep generative models, neural data compression, representation learning, compressibility and learnability, and neural network compression.
cl: Understand source coding theory and representative source coding algorithms.
Understand representative deep generative models.
Have in-depth knowledge of deep lossless and lossy data compression.
Have in-depth knowledge of the relationship between data compressibility and learnability.
Implement deep data compression algorithms and deep generative models.

ELEC5460.d: Stochastic Optimization plays a critical role in radio resource optimization of wireless networks, optimal control theory as well as financial engineering (portfolio optimization). This course will focus on the stochastic optimization theory and the application to the design and optimization of next generation wireless systems and federated learning applications. Topics covered include (A) Physical Layer Modeling: review of information theory for wireless fading channels, MIMO spatial diversity and spatial multiplexing, (B) Theory of Stochastic Optimization: classifications and motivating examples of stochastic optimizations [Type I stochastic Optimization and Type II stochastic optimization problems], theory of Stochastic Approximation, Stochastic Gradient, (C) Applications of Type I SO: Robust optimizations and Federated Learning: (D) Applications of Type II SO: Markov Decision Process, Stochastic Stability and Delay-optimal wireless resource control.
cl: Learn the basic theory of stochastic optimization.
Learn the basic comm and information theory for the sake of modeling of the PHY.
Learn the basic techniques of stochastic optimization formulation for comm-related problems.
Learn the basic techniques of stochastic optimization algorithm designs.

ELEC5470.d: Convex optimization theory with applications to communication systems and signal processing: convex sets/functions/problems; Lagrange duality and KKT conditions; saddle points and minimax problems; numerical algorithms; primal/dual decomposition methods. Applications: filter design; robust beamforming; power control in wireless systems; design of MIMO systems; GP duality in information theory; network utility maximization. For PG students in second year or above.
cl: Learn the basic theory of convex optimization.
Read a paper and understand the optimization component in a critical way.
Learn fundamental optimization techniques such as majorization-minimization method, robust optimization, sparse optimization, low-rank optimization, SDP relaxation, and decomposition methods.

Learn specific applications such as low-rank optimization for matrix completion, portfolio optimization, sparse regression in index tracking, SDP relaxation for maximum likelihood detection, graph learning from data, Internet as a convex optimization problem, support vector machine for classification, etc.
Deal with a new problem using the learned optimization tools.

ELEC5510.d: DC-DC conversion: topologies, continuous and discontinuous conduction modes, steady state analysis, loop gain analysis and relevant mathematical tools, stability and compensation; AC-DC conversion: power factor correctors.
cl: Analyze and design the power stage of switch mode power converters.
Analyze and design the feedback compensator of switch mode power converters.
Apply and understand the limitation of averaging techniques in modeling a periodically switching system.

ELEC5520.d: Integrated circuit techniques for power management components such as voltage references, linear voltage regulators, low dropout regulators, switch mode power converters and switched-capacitor power converters.
cl: Analyze and design power management integrated circuits and systems.
Use simulation tools to help design power management integrated circuits and systems.
Communicate effectively design choices and considerations via written reports.

ELEC5530.d: The course aims to systematically introduce major issues of mixed-signal circuit designs and their applications in bio-medical and sensory systems. The first half course is dedicated to mixed-signal IC design. The course starts with 2 review classes on OPAMP design, filter design and circuit noise. Then, the course covers topics on pipelined ADC, Sigma-delta ADC, and SAR ADC. The second half course is dedicated to sensory and bio-medical IC design. The topics include bio-potential detection, implants, DNA detection, CCD, CMOS imaging, and CT/SPECT.
cl: Demonstrate in-depth understanding of fundamental theories of advanced mixed-signal IC design, and their application to critical mixed-signal circuit blocks.
Demonstrate understanding of the technological status of mixed-signal IC design field.
Execute critical analysis of state-of-the-art mixed-signal IC designs.
Develop skills of mixed-signal IC circuits design through practicing design projects in the course.

ELEC5550.d: The course introduces Electronic Design Automation (EDA) techniques for VLSI digital IC design. The modern RTL to GDS-II design flow and related tools will be explained in detail. Classical automated algorithms adopted in logic synthesis, floorplanning, placement, clock tree synthesis (CTS), routing, etc. will be covered. Simulation and optimization techniques of key IC design objectives, including recent research on AI-assisted EDA, will be presented.
cl: Understand the RTL to GDS-II VLSI digital design flow and implement any given design with this flow.
Understand the simulation and optimization techniques for key IC design objectives and constraints and apply EDA tools to simulate and optimize any given design.
Understand key design stages including logic synthesis, floorplanning, placement, CTS, routing, etc. and use EDA tools to control design trade-offs at each stage.
Understand data structure and algorithms related to digital IC design and implementation.
Develop algorithms for key IC design topics and stages, including logic synthesis, floorplanning, placement, CTS, routing, etc.
Be familiar with recent research topics and works on AI-assisted EDA.

ELEC5600.d: Introduces modern system theory, with applications to control, signal processing and related topics.  Basic system concepts, state-space and I/O representation, properties of linear systems, controllability, observability, minimality, transfer-function matrices, state and output feedback, stability, observers, optimal regulators.
cl: Get acquainted with advanced linear algebra applicable to a broad range of engineering problems.
Get trained in rigorous mathematical reasoning.
Learn the basic concepts and techniques of dynamical system theory.

ELEC5621.d: Biorobotics is an interdisciplinary field that encompasses biomedical engineering, cybernetics, robotics, and more. This course aims to provide an introduction to the fundamental concepts and knowledge of biorobots. It will cover the description and analysis of biorobots with various types of nature-inspired locomotion and behavior. Additionally, it will explore different architectures and scales of biorobots; and discuss advanced techniques and interdisciplinary knowledge required for their development.
cl: Explain the fundamental concepts, terminology, and development trends of biorobotics.
Analyze the mechanisms, kinematics, and dynamics of representative biorobotic systems.
Compare different actuation, sensing, and control methods used in conventional and bioinspired robots.
Evaluate the design principles of biorobots with different locomotion modes and architectures, including terrestrial, swimming, flying, soft, modular, and micro/nano robots.
Critique and present research articles and technical developments in the field of biorobotics.
Apply fundamental principles of biorobotics to analyze or address practical engineering problems.

ELEC5630.d: This course focuses on the fundamental mathematical and physical principles of computer vision. It begins by introducing the physical imaging process, encompassing crucial subjects such as color, polarization, radiometry, reflectance models, and photometric methods. Subsequently, it explores the realm of geometric multi-view vision, encompassing topics like features, multi-view stereo, optical flow, structure-from-motion, visual SLAM, and NeRF. Finally, the course delves into the domain of learning-based methods including classification, segmentation, detection, and diffusion models.
cl: Understand the principles of physically based computer vision.
Develop algorithms to solve radiometric vision problems, such as photometric stereo.
Understand the principles of multiple view geometry.
Develop algorithms to solve 3D vision problems such as visual SLAM, SfM, and depth estimation.

ELEC5640.d: Extensive introduction to robot manipulation theory from a geometric viewpoint. Rigid-body kinematics; spatial and body representation of rigid-body velocities; coordinate transformations; forward kinematics of open-chain manipulators; solution of inverse kinematics; robot workspaces; nonlinear decoupling control and force control.
cl: Understand the fundamentals of robot kinematics and dynamics.
Understand the basics of robotic planning and control.
Implement robotic solutions on real robot platforms.
Advance technical writing and presentation skills.

ELEC5650.d: The course gives an introduction to the analysis and design of sensing, estimation and control systems in a networked setting. It consists of three parts: the first part introduces necessary background knowledge in communication networks, sensor networks, linear state estimation, MAP and ML estimators, Kalman filtering, and modern control theory; the second part focuses on analysis of network effect to remote state estimation and control; the third part presents some advanced topics including distributed state estimation and resource allocation through scheduling.
cl: Understand critical issues in modern networked control applications.
Distinguish the differences between MAP, ML, MMSE, and LMMSE estimators and know their respective application scenorios.
Design a stabilizing controller for a linear Gaussian control systems using Kalman filter and LQR regulator.
Quantify data packet drop rate and maximum delays which may lead to instability of a networked control system.

ELEC5660.d: This course gives a comprehensive introduction to aerial robots. The goal of this course is to expose students to relevant mathematical foundations and algorithms, and train them to develop real-time software modules for aerial robotic systems. Topics to be covered include rigid-body dynamics, system modeling, control, trajectory planning, sensor fusion, and vision-based state estimation. Students will complete a series of projects which combine into an aerial robot that is capable of vision-based autonomous indoor navigation.
cl: Recognize the history and development of aerial robotics.
Explain fundamentals in rigid body dynamics and aerial robot modeling.
Explain computer vision and state estimation techniques for aerial robots.
Implement trajectory planning and feedback control methods for aerial robots.
Implement real-time visual-inertial state estimators for aerial robots.
Analyze performance of algorithm implementations, and improve performance in an iterative manner.
Design and construct a complete autonomous aerial robot system under resource constraints.
Debug and fix real-time robotics system.

ELEC5680.d: This course focuses on advanced deep learning architectures and their applications in various areas. Specifically, the topics include various deep neural network architectures with applications in computer vision, signal processing, graph analysis, and natural language processing. Different state-of-the-art neural network models will be introduced, including graph neural networks, normalizing flows, point cloud models, sparse convolutions,and neural architecture search. The students have the opportunities to implement deep learning models for some AI-related tasks such as visual perception, image processing and generation, graph processing, speech enhancement, sentiment classification, and novel view synthesis.
cl: Understand a broad range of advanced deep learning models.
Have in-depth knowledge of the differences and similarities of deep learning architectures in various areas.
Apply learned deep learning models to solve a problem of interests with a written technical report and presentation.
Write programs in Tensorflow or Pytorch to implement several given deep neural network architectures.
Combine different neural network architectures to solve a problem.

ELEC5690.d: This course provides an introduction to the latest advancements in the broad area of artificial intelligence and its applications in healthcare. It covers basic concepts of deep learning as well as advanced approaches for analyzing diverse healthcare data, including medical images, clinical reports, and biological data. Through hands-on homework projects, students are expected to demonstrate their capability in applying fundamental deep learning techniques to tackle various real-world healthcare problems and challenges.
cl: Deploy deep learning algorithms to perform fundamental image recognition tasks using PyTorch or TensorFlow.
Gain a solid understanding of the latest advancements in Artificial Intelligence.
Acquire a foundational understanding of the challenges faced in healthcare problems.
Obtain the basic skills required to solve healthcare issues using AI techniques.
Develop the ability to execute projects utilizing AI to address real-world healthcare problems.

ELEC5810.d: This is an introductory course on computational biology at the molecular level. It will cover basic biological knowledge, important biological questions, common data acquisition techniques, popular data analysis algorithms and their applications. The major content of this course is computation-oriented.
cl: Understand the fundamentals of bioinformatics.
Demonstrate mastery of, and critical understanding of, relevant scientific literature related to bioinformatics.
Summarize the key points from related literature, make comparisons among different papers, and carry out insightful discussions.

ELEC5820.d: Introduction to Microfluidics and Biosensors; Overview of microfabrication materials & techniques; microfluidic principles; miniaturized biosensors; micro total analysis system (µTAS) & lab-on-a-chip (LOC) for clinical and research applications.
cl: Describe core concepts in the field of Microfluidics & Biosensors.
Describe trends and motivations in the field of Microfluidics & Biosensors.
Analyze/critique research articles in the field of Microfluidics & Biosensors.
Formulate a potential solution for a clinical problem using Microfluidics & Biosensors.

ELEC5900.d: The course provides a high-level description of modern engineering research practices. It covers topics including research mentality, the scientific method, evaluating research topics, literature search, report writing, presenting data, publication, research management, research ethics and technology transfer.
cl: Describe the scientific method for doing research.
Distinguish and categorize different types of researches.
Evaluate the quality of research papers.
Develop a research proposal independently.
Identify different components in a published paper.
Write a critical review of a research paper.
Analyze the arguments concerning research ethics.
Explain the process of technology transfer.

ELEC6770.d: This one-credit course aims at providing research postgraduate students with basic training in teaching skills, research management, career development, and related professional skills. This course consists of a number of mini-workshops. Some department-specific workshops will be coordinated by Department of ECE. Graded PP, P or F.
cl: Acquire teaching skills, research management, career development, and related professional skills.

ELEC6900.d: Selected topics in electronic and computer engineering studied under the supervision of a faculty member. Graded P or F.
cl: Acquire knowledge of special topics related to electronic and computer enginnering.

ELEC6910-6940.d: Selected topics of current interest. May be repeated for credit, if different topics are covered.
cl: Acquire knowledge of special topics related to electronic and computer enginnering.

ELEC6950.d: Series of seminar topics presented by students, faculty and guest speakers. Graded P or F.
cl: Acquire, enhance, and practice presentation skills.

ELEC6990.d: Master's thesis research supervised by a faculty member.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.
cl: Carry out Master's thesis research supervised by a faculty member.
Defend the thesis research conducted by the Thesis Examination Committee.

ELEC7990.d: Original and independent doctoral thesis research.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.
cl: Carry out original and independent doctoral thesis research.
Defend the thesis research conducted by the Thesis Examination Committee.
